id_and_class.summary: Franz Brentano holds that intentionality, being directed at an object, is the mark of the mental: every mental act presents something. Each act is also aware of itself, taking itself as a ‘secondary object’ within one undivided act, so consciousness is built into the act rather than added by a second, higher-order state.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a structured field of mental acts, each directed at a primary object (a sound, a proposition, a person) and at the same time incidentally aware of itself.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Brentano separates mental from physical phenomena by intentionality: every mental phenomenon contains an object within itself and no physical phenomenon does. He leaves causal and physiological conditions to genetic psychology, which he sharply distinguishes from his descriptive project.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not addressed (Brentano describes the structure of consciousness and sets aside its physiological origins)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Intentionality, which Brentano called ‘intentional in-existence’, defines the mental, and its object need not exist (one can fear a fictional monster). Subjectivity comes from the secondary-object structure: hearing a sound is, in the same act, an awareness of the hearing.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Sensory qualities such as colors and sounds are the primary objects of sensory acts, which Brentano calls physical phenomena. What makes the experience conscious is the act’s awareness of itself, not a private container of qualia.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Mental acts, their intentional objects (existent or not), and a unified present consciousness whose parts are only conceptually distinct.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Inner perception, an immediate and infallible awareness that accompanies every act. Inner observation, attending to one’s own act as a target, is impossible because attention alters or destroys the act.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three irreducible classes of acts, with presentations as the base: presentations, judgments (affirming or denying), and phenomena of love and hate. Each act has a primary and a secondary object, which are parts separable in thought but not in reality.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; intentionality; self-awareness; unity of consciousness
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The secondary-object doctrine: every act is directed at its primary object and at itself, making consciousness intrinsic to the act (a same-order account).
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Inner perception gives immediate, infallible self-knowledge, which Brentano takes to ground psychology as a science.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Present consciousness forms a single real unity whose parts can be distinguished only in thought.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Every act presents an object, and judgments and emotions build on presentations by affirming, denying, loving, or hating what is presented.
core_claims_and_evidence: Intentional directedness is present in every mental phenomenon and in no physical phenomenon, so it can define the mental.
A conscious act is aware of itself in the same act, so no higher-order state is required.
Inner perception cannot become inner observation, because turning attention on an act alters it.
There are no unconscious mental states; mental and conscious are co-extensive.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Descriptive psychology (first-person analysis of acts and their structure)

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Husserl rejected two central claims: that mental acts stand before us as objects of inner perception, and that inner perception is infallible. Zahavi, following the Heidelberg School, argues that Brentano models consciousness on awareness of an object and so brings back the subject-object split. Antonelli argues the self-representational reading of Brentano imports a foreign notion of object and risks a regress.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Kriegel calls the denial of unconscious mental states the system’s least defensible element, though he thinks it can be removed without much damage. Interpreters still dispute whether the primary and secondary awareness are strictly identical (Kriegel), one-level and adverbial (Thomasson), or a fusion of a state with an evident cognition of it (Textor).
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a descriptive psychology that brackets metaphysics. Its claims of infallible self-knowledge and no unconscious mind clash with later psychology.
